final_answer: Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible along a branch before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion), while breadth-first search (BFS) explores all neighbors at the current depth before moving deeper, using a queue. DFS can find a path quickly but may miss shorter paths, while BFS guarantees the shortest path in an unweighted graph. You choose DFS for tasks like cycle detection, topological sorting, or solving mazes, and BFS when you need the shortest path or level-order traversal. Safe.
